sentences.text: This giant dinosaur reached an estimated length of twenty meters, or sixty-six feet.
It is distinguished from other sauropods by possessing two separate hollow spaces on the transverse processes of its front back vertebrae.
Among turiasaurs, it stands alone in having a clear ridge running down the middle of its very first back spines.
German geologist Wilhelm Bornhardt first found two sauropod vertebrae near Nambango in 1911.
Werner Janensch described these initial finds in 1929 without naming them, until José Fernando Bonaparte, Wolf-Dieter Heinrich, and Rupert Wild formally named the genus in 2000.
The type specimen consists of two anterior dorsal vertebrae from the Upper Saurian Bed.
Tendaguria is a highly derived sauropod in which the axial musculature has likely shifted position to the dorsal surface of the transverse processes.
Mannion et al. initially placed Tendaguria in Eusauropoda in 2013, but later assigned it to Turiasauria in 2019.
Found in Tanzania within the Tendaguru Formation, this animal lived during the Tithonian stage, between 149.2 and 143.1 million years ago.
Due to its unique morphology, Tendaguria was originally classified as Sauropoda incertae sedis, with authors even creating a separate family, Tendaguriidae.
